about.title: Sand City Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Sand City is small — a few hundred residents between the dunes and Highway 1 — and a death here is felt on every block. For 2025, the most recent final crash year, the public record shows no injury collisions and no traffic deaths. Even so, Sand City families face sudden loss: on SR-1 or its southbound lanes, on California Avenue during the Wednesday morning commute, at work, or in a hospital elsewhere in Monterey County. California treats wrongful death as a civil action, separate from any criminal case. Only certain people may bring the claim — a spouse or domestic partner and children first, then specific dependents and heirs — and it generally must be filed within two years of the death, sooner when a government entity is involved. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the love, companionship and guidance that cannot be replaced. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm; we connect you with an independent attorney who works on contingency.

whyChoose.title: What matters in a California wrongful death case

items.title: Standing is limited under California law
items.desc: A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children have the first right to file; certain dependents and heirs may follow. An attorney can confirm who in your family is eligible before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines are short and can be shorter
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death, but if a public agency — say, the one responsible for a stretch of SR-1 — is involved, the window closes much sooner. Early guidance protects that timeline.

items.title: Losses go beyond the funeral bill
items.desc: California allows recovery of burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. A civil claim proceeds independently of any criminal prosecution.

items.question: Sand City recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Can my family still have a claim?
items.answer: Yes. Where you live does not decide whether a claim exists; what matters is where and how the death happened. Sand City residents commute along SR-1 and work across Monterey County, and a fatal crash, workplace incident or act of medical negligence anywhere in California can support a wrongful death action. An attorney can review the facts and tell you honestly whether a claim is worth pursuing.

items.question: The driver is facing criminal charges. Do we wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No, and waiting can hurt you. A wrongful death lawsuit is a separate civil matter with its own two-year deadline that keeps running regardless of what the district attorney does. Evidence from the criminal case may help, but your family's claim stands on its own.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring the claim, and what if there is a disagreement?
items.answer: California gives priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children; if none exist, certain dependents and heirs may file. Because all eligible heirs are usually joined in a single action, families sometimes need help sorting out roles. An independent attorney can explain each person's rights without taking sides.
